summary: Hamilton County, NY: 18-ft wood lookout built 1909, 50-ft steel tower from 1916, removed by DEC in Dec 1976; no official source describes the summit today, but a 2017 forum trip report describes relics and an overgrown summit.

facts.design: 18-foot wooden tower (1909); 50-foot steel Aermotor LL25 tower from 1916
facts.status_note: The 50-foot steel tower was removed in December 1976. No official source found describes the summit today. A 2017 forum trip report describes relics of the old tower and an overgrown summit with no views.

staffing.status: closed; no observers named in the sources read

access.note: The peak lies in the Silver Lake Wilderness (forest preserve). A 2004 forum post says the trail is on private property. A 2017 forum post says private property on the west side ruled out that approach and that the area where the old trail had been is heavily posted; the same poster then reached the summit by an off-trail route from the east. No official access source found.

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb. A 2013 forum post describes the old trail as being reclaimed by the forest. A 2017 forum post describes an off-trail climb to the summit and says the top is overgrown with no views. No current trail or access rules were found.

facts.agency: Forest, Fish and Game Commission (1909); New York State Environmental Conservation Department (1976 removal)

events.note: 18-foot wooden tower built in October 1909 by the Forest, Fish and Game Commission; a 1910 annual report gives the cost as $694.51
Wooden tower replaced by a 50-foot steel tower (Aermotor LL25 per Wikipedia)
A new cabin was erected at the site
Closed at the end of the 1971 fire lookout season because aerial detection had improved (Wikipedia). A December 1976 report says it had been closed for six years, which points to about 1970
DEC removed the tower in early December 1976 because it did not conform to forever wild rules; accounts of how it came down differ
The cabin was to remain on the peak until summer 1977 and then be removed (plan reported in December 1976)

corrections.why: 5.5 m (18 ft) is the October 1909 wooden tower. The 1916 steel tower that stood until the December 1976 removal was 50 ft (about 15.2 m).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts (quoting The Post-Standard) and the Weekly Express place the take-down in early December 1976. Wikipedia says around 1977, and a 2004 forum post says 1977 or 1978. The story leads with the December 1976 reports and mentions the later dates.
Wikipedia says the tower closed at the end of the 1971 fire lookout season. A December 1976 report says it had been closed for six years, which points to about 1970. The story gives both.
Wikipedia gives 3,215 feet. A 1976 report quoted by Forest Lookouts gives 3,250 feet. The story gives both.

Sources name different nearby hamlets: Wells (Wikipedia), Lake Pleasant (the 1909 report and the Weekly Express) and Speculator (the 1976 report). The firelookout.org coordinates sit within a few hundred metres of Wikipedia's GNIS coordinates, so the site location agrees and only the town names differ.

The Post-Standard says crews unbolted two legs and pulled the tower over with a power winch. The Weekly Express says a strong wind had twisted it, so it was lowered with cat and guy ropes. Both describe a crew take-down; the story gives both accounts.

notes_for_editor: Build date, the 1916 steel tower and the December 1976 take-down are well documented through newspaper quotes on Forest Lookouts and the Weekly Express article. The 1977 New York Times archive item returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Current condition and access rest on anecdotal forum posts from 2004, 2013 and 2017; no official source found. The Weekly Express credits a photo to the Speculator Lake Pleasant Historical Society, but no image URL was found, so no photos were added. A forum poster recommends Martin Podskoch's book Adirondack Fire Towers: Their History and Lore, Southern Districts, which may hold observer details; it was not read. Facebook pages did not load. Grokipedia was not used.
